item.title: INDUCE Definition & Meaning - Merriam-Webster
item.description: Inducing is usually gentle persuasion; you may, for instance, induce a friend to go to a concert, or induce a child to stop crying. An inducement is something that might lure you to do something, though inducements are occasionally a bit menacing, like the Godfather's offer that you can't refuse.

item.title: INDUCE | English meaning - Cambridge Dictionary
item.description: They induced her to take the job by offering her a bonus. If doctors induce labor, they cause a baby to be born before its natural time.

item.description: INDUCED definition: brought about, produced, or caused, especially artificially (often used in combination). See examples of induced used in a sentence.

item.title: Induced - definition of induced by The Free Dictionary
item.description: To lead or move, as to a course of action, by influence or persuasion. See Synonyms at persuade. 2. To bring about or stimulate the occurrence of; cause: a drug used to induce labor. 3. To infer by inductive reasoning. 4. Physics. a. To produce (an electric current or a magnetic charge) by induction. b.

item.description: (in combination) Brought about; caused to happen.

item.title: INDUCE Definition & Meaning | Dictionary.com
item.description: to lead or move by persuasion or influence, as to some action or state of mind. to induce a person to buy a raffle ticket. to bring about, produce, or cause. That medicine will induce sleep. Physics. to produce (an electric current) by induction.

item.title: Induce - Definition, Meaning & Synonyms | Vocabulary.com
item.description: To induce is to move or lead someone to action. A promise of a lollipop can induce a toddler to do just about anything, even sit down and be polite to Aunt Edna. Older kids need something more substantial.
